subject: Maths
title: Writing and representing vectors
subtitle: Vectors · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can write vectors using column notation and represent them on a grid.

key_vocab.definition: A vector describes a movement with both magnitude (size) and direction. We write column vectors as (x, y) where x is the horizontal movement and y is the vertical movement.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can write vectors using column notation and represent them on a grid.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: vector -- A vector describes a movement with both magnitude (size) and direction. We write column vectors as (x, y) where x is the horizontal movement and y is the vertical movement.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
A column vector gives horizontal then vertical displacement. Equal vectors have the same column vector regardless of starting point.
vector = (horizontal, vertical)
Right and up are positive; left and down are negative

Key examples:
  ✓ (3, 2) means 3 right and 2 up  (positive components)
  ✓ (-1, 4) means 1 left and 4 up  (negative x means left)
  ✓ (3, 2) and (3, 2) drawn at different points are equal  (same magnitude and direction)
  ✗ (3, 2) means 3 up and 2 right  (x is horizontal (first), y is vertical (second))
  ✗ (2, 5) and (-2, -5) are the same vector  (they have opposite directions)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – writing a column vector
  Write the vector that moves from A(1, 3) to B(4, 7) as a column vector.
  Horizontal: 4 - 1 = 3 (right)
  Vertical: 7 - 3 = 4 (up)
  Column vector: (3, 4)
  (3, 4)
  (Subtract the start coordinates from the end coordinates.)

Example 2 – negative components
  Write the vector from P(5, 6) to Q(2, 1).
  Horizontal: 2 - 5 = -3 (left)
  Vertical: 1 - 6 = -5 (down)
  Column vector: (-3, -5)
  (-3, -5)
  (Negative values show movement left or down.)

sections.title: Writing column vectors
sections.content:
Write each movement as a column vector.

(a) 3 right, 5 up
(b) 2 left, 4 up
(c) 6 right, 1 down
(d) 4 left, 3 down

sections.title: From coordinates
sections.content:
Find the column vector from the first point to the second.

(a) (1, 2) to (4, 6)
(b) (5, 7) to (2, 3)
(c) (0, 0) to (6, -2)
(d) (3, 8) to (3, 1)

sections.title: Drawing vectors
sections.content:
Starting from the given point, state the end point after applying the vector.

(a) Start (2, 3), vector (4, 1)
(b) Start (5, 6), vector (-3, 2)
(c) Start (0, 4), vector (2, -4)
(d) Start (7, 1), vector (-5, -1)

sections.title: Mixed vector problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Write the return vector (opposite) of (3, -2)
(b) A to B is (4, 5). B to C is (1, -3). Find A to C.
(c) P to Q is (-2, 6). What is Q to P?
(d) Vector (a, 3) moves (2, 1) to (5, 4). Find a.
(e) Are (4, -1) and (-4, 1) equal, opposite, or neither?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ (3, -2) means 3 right and 2 down
✗ (3, -2) means 3 up and 2 left
✓ Two vectors with the same column vector are equal regardless of position
✗ (0, 5) means no movement at all
✓ The negative of (a, b) is (-a, -b)
